item.title: LinkedIn Now Catches AI Slop With 94% Precision: What Founders Should Change
item.description: LinkedIn's AI slop classifiers now check every post shown outside your network with 94% precision, and slop gets about 40% fewer views. Here's what founders should change.

item.title: From 2 Connections to 83,285 Post Impressions in 7 Days
item.description: Victor Kimotho started the week with 2 connections. Seven days later his posts for work.ke had 83,285 impressions, and 98% of the impressions on two of them came from outside his network.

item.title: OpenAI Is Halving Its 200$ Plan: Budget for AI Price Rises
item.description: OpenAI keeps its 200$ plan at 200$ but halves the usage from October 30, and adds a 500$ tier. Founders running on one AI subscription should plan for higher costs.

item.title: Stop Asking for 15 Minutes in the Gulf
item.description: A 15-minute call request feels efficient, but in the Gulf it tells a C-level buyer your time and your offer are both cheap.

item.title: AI Agents Need a Leash: What OpenAI's Pause Means for Founders
item.description: OpenAI paused training after its AI agents probed US government sites in unexpected ways. The lesson for founders is about scope, not fear.

item.title: Silence Is Not Rejection in Gulf Enterprise Sales
item.description: A three-month silence from a Riyadh executive taught me the difference between chasing a deal and staying anchored to it.

item.title: Stop Selling Like a Petitioner in the Gulf
item.description: Top executives in Dubai, Riyadh and Doha are surrounded by vendors who agree with everything they say, and they are exhausted by it.

item.title: The Best Time to Send B2B Outreach in the Gulf: Why 9 AM on Monday Fails
item.description: Most LinkedIn and email outreach in Dubai and Riyadh lands during the wrong hour of a crowded morning. Two send windows get read and answered far more often.

item.title: From 2% to 30%: How One Sentence Changes B2B Reply Rates
item.description: A field lesson from B2B outreach campaigns in Dubai, Riyadh and Singapore: why a relevant personal signal matters more than a polished generic message.

item.title: Dubai and Riyadh Are Not the Same B2B Market
item.description: Dubai and Riyadh are only 90 minutes apart by plane, but the same LinkedIn message should not be sent to both markets.

item.title: From cold profile to 200 enterprise meetings: a LinkedIn growth case study
item.description: Most LinkedIn profiles in B2B look the same. A headshot, a job title, a list of previous roles. No clear message. No reason for anyone to connect, follow, or reach out. That was the starting point when I began working with the founder of a Dubai-based AI software company serving the GCC retail market. His LinkedIn had around 400 connections. Mostly old colleagues and people he had met at events. No strategy. No outreach. No pipeline coming from the platform.

item.title: The LinkedIn profile optimization guide for B2B outreach
item.description: Most people treat LinkedIn profile optimization as a one-time task they do when they first create an account. They upload a photo, write a headline, add their work history and move on. Then they launch an outreach campaign and wonder why the results are disappointing.

item.title: The 5 mistakes B2B founders make in their first outreach campaign
item.description: Most founders launch their first LinkedIn outreach campaign with good intentions and poor results. The problem is rarely the product. It is almost always the execution. Here are the five mistakes that kill response rates before the conversation even starts.

item.title: Why your LinkedIn profile matters before outreach starts
item.description: Outreach does not happen only inside the message box. It also happens on the profile page, where trust is either supported or damaged.
